summary: Provisioned a LUKS2-encrypted volume on node1 (Alpine 3.23), mounted at /srv/secure, that unlocks and mounts automatically at boot with no manual steps. Because node1 had no spare block device, the volume is backed by a 512MB image file (/var/lib/crypt/secure.img) attached via loop device, LUKS2-formatted with a random keyfile generated on the node (/etc/keys/secure.key, mode 400). A custom OpenRC service (/etc/init.d/secure-crypt) losetups the image and opens the LUKS mapping before localmount runs; /etc/fstab mounts /dev/mapper/secure at /srv/secure. Discovered and fixed a boot-ordering bug: the stock cryptsetup-openrc 'dmcrypt' service declares 'before fsck', which conflicted with the 'after root' override needed to avoid racing the root filesystem's read-only-to-read-write remount (root remounts rw seconds after boot, and the loop device inherited read-only if created before that). Root cause was confirmed via dmesg timestamps showing the loop device created before the rw remount. Replaced the generic dmcrypt config with the dedicated secure-crypt service (need/after root, before localmount), eliminating the dependency cycle. Verified via three reboot cycles: boot 1 showed the volume mounted but stuck read-only (bug found); boot 2 (after adding rc_after=root to dmcrypt) still failed due to the cycle; boot 3 (after switching to the custom secure-crypt service) succeeded — volume auto-unlocked, mounted read-write, and a file written before the reboot was present and additional writes succeeded post-boot, all without any manual commands. Boot identity (kernel boot_id) changed across all three restarts, confirming genuine reboots, and the encrypted volume's health/data was independently reverified after the final restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Alpine 3.23.3, single root disk (vda), no spare block device, no cryptsetup installed
Installed cryptsetup and cryptsetup-openrc via apk
Created 512MB backing image /var/lib/crypt/secure.img and 512-byte random keyfile /etc/keys/secure.key (chmod 400)
Formatted the image as LUKS2 via a loop device and opened/mkfs.ext4'd the mapped device 'secure'
Mounted /srv/secure manually, wrote a test file, verified read/write, then unmounted/closed/detached to reset to a clean pre-boot-like state
Initial attempt: added target=secure to /etc/conf.d/dmcrypt and enabled dmcrypt+localmount in the boot runlevel
Rebooted node1 (boot_id changed 06001d94->95ee94ef) and found /srv/secure auto-mounted but stuck read-only
Diagnosed via dmesg timestamps: loop device was created (and inherited RO) before the root filesystem's ro->rw remount completed

Attempted fix: enabled root/fsck services and added rc_after=root to dmcrypt config; rebooted again (boot_id 95ee94ef->6aedd568) and confirmed the fix did not work due to a dependency cycle (dmcrypt declares 'before fsck', root needs fsck, dmcrypt now needed 'after root' -> cycle silently broken by OpenRC)
Removed the dmcrypt-based config entirely and wrote a dedicated /etc/init.d/secure-crypt OpenRC service (need/after root, before localmount) that losetups the image and opens the LUKS mapping
Enabled secure-crypt in the boot runlevel, verified no dependency cycle via /run/openrc/deptree, and manually validated the service brings up a read/write mapping
Wrote a persistence marker file into /srv/secure, reset to clean state, and performed a final reboot (boot_id 6aedd568->30f343a0)

Verified after the final reboot: secure-crypt/root/fsck/localmount all started, /srv/secure auto-mounted read-write, prior test file content intact, and new writes succeeded without any manual intervention

evidence.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot (final working config)

evidence.requirement: Diagnosis of read-only boot bug and root cause
evidence.summary: dmesg timestamps showed the loop device (and resulting dm-crypt mapping) was created read-only because it was set up before the root filesystem's ro->rw remount completed at boot

evidence.requirement: Node restart 1: baseline capture, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id 06001d94-1283-4f5d-8928-43ca083781c0, issued backgrounded reboot with returned acknowledgement, polled through disconnect, and confirmed new boot_id 95ee94ef-f4a4-42a7-b8fe-85340eb182d9 after recovery

evidence.requirement: Node restart 1: post-restart service/data verification (revealed bug)
evidence.summary: Post-reboot check showed dmcrypt started and /srv/secure mounted with prior test file intact, but mounted read-only, prompting the fix cycle

evidence.requirement: Node restart 3 (final): full recovery proof — service health, read-write mount, data integrity, new writes
evidence.summary: Post-final-reboot check confirmed fsck/root/secure-crypt/localmount all started, /srv/secure auto-mounted rw, the pre-reboot test file 'confirmed-writable' content was intact, and a brand-new file could be written and removed without any manual unlock steps
